Authentication

# Authentication

Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.

The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.

## Getting Your API Token

API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.

Click your **profile icon** in the top-right corner and select **API Tokens** (or go to [app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens](app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens) ).

Click **New Token** .

Enter a descriptive **token name** and choose an **expiration date** .

Click **Create** , then copy and securely store the generated token.

Keep Your Token Secure

Your API token grants access to your account and plan resources. Never expose your token in client-side code (like browsers or mobile apps), and store it securely in an environment variable or server configuration.

## Authenticating Requests

Include your API token in the `x-api-token` HTTP header on every request:

```
x-api-token :  <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```

### Marketplace Endpoints

For [Marketplace endpoints](app.mrscraper.com/marketplace) , authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 `Authorization` header with a Bearer token:

```
Authorization :  Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```

## Verify Token

To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the [`/subscription-accounts`](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/authentication/verify-token) endpoint:

```
curl  -X  GET  "api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts"  \   -H  "accept: application/json"  \   -H  "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

## Analytics Authentication

[Analytics endpoints](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/analytic/status) authenticate using the same `x-api-token` header as all other API endpoints.

When querying analytics, you can also pass the `apiTokenName` query parameter to filter status data for a specific token by the name you assigned when creating it:

```
curl  -X  GET  "api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/analytic/statuses?domain=example.com&startDate=2026-04-12%2000:00:00&endDate=2026-04-13%2023:59:59&apiTokenName=YOUR_TOKEN_NAME"  \   -H  "accept: application/json"  \   -H  "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

MCP Server

MCP Server

Official MrScraper MCP server for web scraping, structured data extraction, and Google search. Connect AI clients or run the open-source server locally.
MrScraper MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper. It connects AI clients to web scraping, structured data extraction, and Google search.
MrScraper MCP server source code on GitHub · Install the @mrscraper/mcp npm package
The server exposes seven tools:
### fetch Fetch page HTML using Web Renderer with browser rendering and proxy routing. ### scrape Extract structured fields, listing records, or site maps with AI agents. ### serp Query Google SERP for structured search engine results and page discovery. ### status Check subscription status, quota usage, rate limits, and token metrics. ### rerun Execute new runs for saved AI or manual scraper configurations. ### results Browse, filter, paginate, and search stored MrScraper result collections. ### result Retrieve full output data and metadata for a single stored result by ID.
Use the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint for a managed connection, or run the published MCP package locally through Streamable HTTP or stdio.

Capabilities

Web Renderer

Fetch a known URL with browser rendering, proxy-country routing, selector waiting, resource controls, and retry limits.

AI Extraction

Extract page fields, repeated listing records, or a site URL map with agent-specific inputs.

Google SERP

Search Google from a query or a complete Google search URL and select JSON or HTML output.

Account Status

Read subscription, quota, token usage, rate limits, and optional domain request outcomes.

Saved Scrapers

Rerun saved AI or manual scraper configurations for one URL or a bulk URL list.

Stored Results

Browse, filter, paginate, and retrieve stored MrScraper results.

Managed Endpoint

Connect to the hosted MCP endpoint through Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in.

Structured Tool Results

Receive a consistent response envelope in MCP structured content.

Requirements

* A MrScraper account
* An MCP client with Streamable HTTP support
* An API key only when the client cannot use OAuth 2.1 or when running the server locally

Quick start with the hosted server

Add the hosted endpoint
Configure a Streamable HTTP server named mrscraper with no credential:
{   "mcpServers" : {     "mrscraper" : {       "type" :  "http" ,       "url" :  "mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"     }   } }
Use this exact URL, including the /mcp path.
Sign in
Connect or reload the MCP server. Your client follows the OAuth 2.1 challenge, opens MrScraper in your browser, and asks you to approve access.
Reload and verify
Reload the client or start a new session, then inspect its MCP tool list. The connection should expose fetch , scrape , serp , status , rerun , results , and result .

...

* Self-hosted Streamable HTTP | Authorization: Bearer <MrScraper API key>
* Local stdio | MRSCRAPER_API_KEY , then MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN
The hosted server publishes OAuth 2.1 protected-resource metadata and challenges unauthenticated clients to start browser sign-in. Access tokens are issued for the exact mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp resource and use scrape:read , scrape:write , and account:read scopes. A tool called without its required scope returns 403 insufficient_scope .
API keys remain supported for clients without OAuth and carry full account authority. Authentication stays at the transport layer; tools never accept credentials as arguments.

Run the MCP server locally

Node.js 20 or newer is required.

Published package over stdio

{   "mcpServers" : {     "mrscraper" : {       "command" :  "npx" ,       "args" : [ "-y" ,  "@mrscraper/mcp@latest" ],       "env" : {         "MRSCRAPER_API_KEY" :  "YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"       }     }   } }

API Overview

# API Overview

Comprehensive documentation for MrScraper's API endpoints, including authentication, pagination, error handling, and scraper management.

## Introduction

The MrScraper API provides a powerful and flexible way to programmatically scrape web pages and retrieve structured data. Built on REST principles, our API offers predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes.

## API Features

### JSON Format

All requests with a payload require `Content-Type: application/json` header. All responses are returned in JSON format.

### Authentication

All API endpoints require authentication using an API token passed in the `x-api-token` header. See the [Authentication](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/authentication) page for details.

### Pagination

List endpoints support pagination to handle large datasets efficiently. See the [Pagination](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/pagination) page for details.

### Response Headers

Track token usage, bandwidth usage, execution runtime, and target status codes in response headers. See the [Response Headers](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/response-headers) page for details.

### Error Handling

The API uses standard HTTP status codes and returns detailed error messages. See the [Error Handling](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/error-handling) page for details.

## Available Endpoints

[### Scraper API Scrape HTML, Markdown, screenshots, JSON, listings, and sitemaps from a single Scraper API endpoint.](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/scraper/web-fetching-scraping) [### Platform Create, rerun, and manage scrapers programmatically with the Platform API.](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/v3/scraper/ai/ai-init)

[Authentication Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.](docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/authentication)

MrScraper MCP Server for Web Scraping and Web Search

MrScraper MCP is the official MrScraper server for the Model Context Protocol . It connects AI assistants to page content and web search through two SDK-compatible tools, plus an account check. Retrieve HTML, Markdown, or screenshots with scraperAPI , discover pages with webSearch , and check your plan and token usage with status .
Use the hosted server with OAuth sign-in, or run the open-source server locally with the @mrscraper/mcp npm package . See the MrScraper MCP documentation for setup instructions and client configurations.
The server exposes three tools:
scraperAPI  webSearch  status

Deployment options

* Option | Endpoint or command | Best for
* Hosted | mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp | A managed Streamable HTTP connection
* Local HTTP | TRANSPORT=http npx -y @mrscraper/mcp@latest | A self-managed HTTP service

...

Connect with an API key instead

An API key still works as a bearer token, which is what self-hosted deployments and non-OAuth clients use:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
Use your client's environment-variable or secret-storage feature so the key stays out of project files. An API key carries your full account authority, so no scope is enforced against it.

Codex

export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY="YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
codex mcp add mrscraper \
  --url mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY
Start Codex from an environment containing MRSCRAPER_API_KEY . Codex stores the environment-variable name in its MCP configuration.

Scraper API

# Scraper API

Build, test, and validate scraping requests in MrScraper's Scraper API, preview results, and generate production-ready API code without coding.

The [**Scraper API**](app.mrscraper.com/scraper-api) lets you build, test, and validate scraping requests without writing any code. It provides an interactive interface for configuring requests, previewing results, and generating production-ready API code.

## What You Can Do

### Test Requests

Send API requests and view results instantly.

### Adjust Parameters

Experiment with extraction settings and options.

### Generate Code

Generate ready-to-use code snippets in multiple languages.

### Preview Responses

Inspect the returned data before building your integration.

## Scraper API Overview

The Scraper API has these main panels:

* **Target URL** : Configure and run the request.
* **Example Code** : Copy generated request code.
* **Extracted Data** : View the response.
* **Settings** : Adjust optional loading, rendering, and extraction options (Basic Settings, Advanced Settings, and Automation).
* **Alert Settings** : Get notified when a scrape returns errors or incomplete data.

## Target URL

In the **Target URL** panel, you configure and run the request:

* Enter the target URL.
* Select **Run** to send the request, or **Reset** to clear the current configuration.
* Select a country to load the page from. (Default to `United States` )

## Example Code

The **Example Code** panel builds an API request from your current configuration and updates it automatically as you make changes. Copy the code and use it directly in your application.

Supported languages:

* cURL
* Python
* JavaScript
* PHP
* Go
* Java
* Ruby
* C#

Agent Integration

You can view the ready-made prompt for your AI coding agent to integrate MrScraper.

## Extracted Data

The **Extracted Data** panel displays the response MrScraper returns after a request completes :

* HTTP status code
* Total runtime
* Token used

Depending on the use case, the response may include:

* Raw HTML
* Markdown
* JSON

Use this panel to confirm the extracted content matches your requirements before you integrate the request into your application.

Info

This panel can also show history of your previous requests and analytic of your requests.

...

### Notification Rate

The **Identifier** sets the key MrScraper uses to group alerts, so the same alert isn't sent repeatedly. **Rate Limit** and **TTL** apply separately to each group.

Scalekit

Scalekit

Connect MrScraper MCP through Scalekit AgentKit to give your AI agents per-user web fetching, web search, and account usage tools.
Scalekit AgentKit offers a MrScraper MCP connector that lets your agents call the MrScraper MCP server on behalf of each of your users. Each user connects their own MrScraper account once through OAuth 2.1. Scalekit stores the token in an encrypted per-user vault, refreshes it automatically, and runs each tool call with that user's credentials, so tokens never enter the LLM context.

Available tools

* Tool | Description
* mrscrapermcp_scraperapi | Fetches a known page as HTML, Markdown, a screenshot, or a combination.
* mrscrapermcp_websearch | Searches the web and returns result URLs, titles, and descriptions.
* mrscrapermcp_status | Reports the account's subscription status, token limit, usage, remaining tokens, and rate limit.
All tools are read-only. To limit what an agent can do, expose only the tools it needs, for example only mrscrapermcp_websearch .

Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have:
* A MrScraper account for each user who will connect.
* A Scalekit account with AgentKit enabled.
* Your Scalekit API credentials from Developers > API Credentials in the Scalekit dashboard.

Integration Steps

Install the Scalekit SDK

Python Node.js
pip  install  scalekit-sdk-python  python-dotenv
npm  install  @scalekit-sdk/node  dotenv

Set Your Credentials

Add your Scalekit credentials to a .env file:
.env
SCALEKIT_ENVIRONMENT_URL =< your-environment-url > SCALEKIT_CLIENT_ID =< your-client-id > SCALEKIT_CLIENT_SECRET =< your-client-secret >

Create the MrScraper MCP Connection

1. In the Scalekit dashboard, open AgentKit > Connections .
2. Create a MrScraper MCP connection and copy its redirect URI.
3. Register an OAuth app with the MrScraper MCP server using that redirect URI, then enter the app's Client ID and Client Secret on the connection.
The connection name you choose is the name your code passes. The examples below use mrscrapermcp .

Authorize a User and Make a First Call

Generate an authorization link for a user, have them sign in to MrScraper, then call a tool with their identifier.
Python Node.js
quickstart.py

results.title: Authenticate Web Data Tools for AI Agents Without Exposing Secrets | MrScraper
excerpts:
If the model never has the key, it cannot leak it.
This guide shows how to set up authentication so the agent can use web data tools without ever seeing a secret.

Two ways to connect

Most teams use one of two patterns:
1. Your backend owns the key. Your server holds a MrScraper API token. The agent calls your tools, and your server calls MrScraper.
2. Each user connects their own account. A person signs in to MrScraper through their MCP client, such as Claude Code or Codex. The client handles the sign-in, and the agent uses that person's access. The next section covers when to use each one.

When should you use API keys or OAuth?

* Use an API key when | Use OAuth when
* Your app calls MrScraper on its own behalf | A person connects their own MrScraper account
* The call runs on your server, a job runner or CI | The call runs from that person's MCP client
* One account pays for and owns the usage | Each person's usage should stay on their account
* You control where the key is stored | You do not want anyone to copy or paste a key

API keys for your backend

MrScraper API tokens are created in the dashboard under API Tokens . Each token has a name and an expiration date. You can create more than one, so you can give each environment or app its own token. See the API token docs for the steps.
The REST API reads the token from the x-api-token header. The Scraper API examples also pass it as a token query parameter. Your server sends both. The agent never sees either.

OAuth for people using MCP clients

The hosted MrScraper MCP server at mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp supports OAuth 2.1. The client opens a browser, the person signs in, and no key is copied anywhere.
To add it in Claude Code:
bash Copy
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user mrscraper mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
To add it in Codex:
bash Copy
codex mcp add mrscraper --url mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
OAuth access uses scopes:
* scrape:read covers the scraperAPI and webSearch tools.
* account:read covers the status tool. If a client calls a tool without the right scope, the server refuses it with a 403 insufficient_scope error. Grant only the scopes a person needs.

When a client does not support OAuth

Some MCP clients cannot do the browser sign-in. For those, the MCP server accepts an API key as a bearer token in the Authorization header. If you run it locally over stdio, it reads the key from the MRSCRAPER_API_KEY environment variable.
Point the client at the variable name, not the value, when it lets you. Codex supports this with a flag:
bash Copy
codex mcp add mrscraper --url mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY
If a client config file must hold the key, keep that file out of version control and readable only by you.

# Overview

Your all-in-one guide to understanding, configuring, and using the MrScraper platform, from your first scrape to AI agents, integrations, and APIs.

Discover how our powerful scraping platform can transform the way you extract data. Whether you're scraping e-commerce product data, collecting job listings, gathering customer reviews for sentiment analysis, or extracting any website content, our AI scrapers and workflows are designed to automate and simplify the process, giving you a powerful edge in any project.

## Start Here

New to MrScraper? These pages get you from sign-up to your first scraped dataset.

### Quickstart

Run your first scraper in a few minutes with a step-by-step walkthrough.

### Web Search

Run a search query and get ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources.

### Scraper API

Test API requests, explore features, and generate code without writing code.

### Token Plan

Learn how tokens work and create an API token for authentication.

### CLI

Retrieve pages, search the web, and check usage from your terminal.

### MCP Server

Connect AI clients to MrScraper for page retrieval, web search, and usage.

### Billing

Understand subscription plans, token usage, and billing cycles.

## Features

Explore MrScraper's key features and tools designed to make data extraction effortless.

### Workflow

Build and customize your own scraper workflow step by step for full control.

### Self-Healing

Let AI generate, repair, and extend workflows when a site changes.

### Workflow API Access

Activate a scraper as an API endpoint and run it programmatically.

### Bulk Scraping

Scrape multiple URLs in one go by uploading a list or Excel file.

### Proxy

Route individual scrapers through proxies to mask your IP and improve reliability.

### Marketplace

Use ready-to-run scrapers for popular websites and common scraping use cases.

### Scheduling

Automate scraper runs on a schedule to keep your data fresh and up to date.

### S3 Storage

Save scraped data straight into y
...
se the right loading path, geo-targeting, retry, and timeout settings.

### Cookie

Use your own cookies to access content behind logins and restrictions.

### Team

Create a team to share scrapers and collaborate on projects.

## Use Cases

Discover how MrScraper can support different real-world scenarios.

### E-Commerce

Scrape product details, pricing, and availability from major e-commerce sites.

### Job Listings

Collect job postings and company data for recruitment or market analysis.

### Sentiment Analysis

Extract and analyze customer feedback to gain insights into sentiment and satisfaction.

### Real Estate

Gather property listings, prices, and market trends from real estate websites.

### Flight Price

...
ents per-user web fetching and search through Scalekit AgentKit.

### Apify

Run MrScraper as Apify Actors and pipe results into the Apify platform.

### ClawHub

Install the MrScraper skill to give your OpenClaw agent reliable web scraping.

## Developer Tools

Work with MrScraper from your terminal, your codebase, or your AI agent. The MrScraper MCP server source code is available on GitHub for local setup, contributions, and issue reports.

### CLI

Scrape pages, extract brand details and JSON, search the web, and check account status from your terminal.

### MCP Server

Let AI agents fetch pages and search Google through the Model Context Protocol.

### Python SDK

```

package.

### API Reference

Explore every endpoint, authentication, pagination, and error handling.

## Residential Proxy

Route your own tools and browsers through our proxy network.

# MCP Server

Official MrScraper MCP server for retrieving web pages, web search, and account usage. Connect AI clients or run the open-source server locally.

MrScraper MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper.
It connects AI clients to web page retrieval, web search, and your account
usage.

The server exposes seven tools:

Use the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint for a managed connection, or run the
published MCP package locally through Streamable HTTP or stdio.

Package information

This page documents `@mrscraper/mcp` version **0.5.0**. Its seven tools share their descriptions, inputs, and defaults with the MrScraper CLI, SDKs, and integrations. 0.5.0 replaced `scraperAPI` with `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, and `getScreenshot`, added `scrapeBrand` and `scrapeJson`, renamed the inputs to camel case, and changed the OAuth scopes. See Migration from the previous tool set.

## Capabilities

### Page Retrieval

Retrieve a known URL as HTML, Markdown, or a screenshot, with optional
browser rendering, real-device routing, proxy controls, selector waiting,
and retry limits.

### Brand and JSON Extraction

Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links, or
structured JSON from a natural-language prompt.

### Web Search

Search the web for ranked results, for a chosen country and up to 100
results at a time.

### Account Status

Read the subscription, token limit, token usage, remaining tokens, and rate
limit.

### Managed Endpoint

Connect to the hosted MCP endpoint through Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1
browser sign-in.

### Structured Tool Results

Receive a consistent response envelope in MCP structured content.

### Interactive Widgets

Render search results and an account usage meter in hosts that support MCP
Apps.

## Requirements

* A MrScraper account
* An MCP client with Streamable HTTP support
* An API key only when the client cannot use
  OAuth 2.1 or when running the server locally

## Quick start with the hosted server

Add the hosted endpoint

Configure a Streamable HTTP server named `mrscraper` with no credential:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Use this exact URL, including the `/mcp` path.

Sign in

Connect or reload the MCP server. Your client follows the OAuth 2.1
challenge, opens MrScraper in your browser, and asks you to approve
`scrape:read` for the six scraping and search tools and `account:read`
for `status`.

Reload and verify

Reload the client or start a new session, then inspect its MCP tool list.
The connection should expose `status`, `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`,
`getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch`.

## Copyable AI setup prompt

```
Connect MrScraper MCP to this agent. Detect the current MCP client and use its native Streamable HTTP setup to add a server named mrscraper at exactly https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp with no static credential. Complete the OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in; if it does not start automatically, use the client's MCP login or authenticate command. Only if the client does not support OAuth, fall back to a MrScraper API key from https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens stored through the client's environment-variable or secret-storage mechanism and sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Reload the MCP client when required, then list the tools and confirm that status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson, and webSearch are available.
```

## Client configuration

Add the hosted URL without a static `Authorization` header, then complete
browser sign-in when the client prompts you.

### Codex

```
codex mcp add mrscraper \
  --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```

Codex uses OAuth by default for Streamable HTTP servers. If browser sign-in does
not start automatically, run `codex mcp login mrscraper`.

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add \
  --transport http \
  --scope user \
  mrscraper https://mcp.mrscr

# Authentication

Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.

The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.

## Getting Your API Token

API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.

Click your **profile icon** in the top-right corner and select **API Tokens** (or go to [app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens](app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens) ).

Click **New Token** .

Enter a descriptive **token name** and choose an **expiration date** .

Click **Create** , then copy and securely store the generated token.

Keep Your Token Secure

Your API token grants access to your account and plan resources. Never
